So this isn't entirely true with corn. (Still a really good quote)

Corn is a "brush" pollinator. You can see for yourself if you plant two corn patches, one with the corn in rows close together, and one with the corn in a single row, with more space. The crowded corn will grow bigger corn. That's because the corn gets pollinated by brushing up against other corn around it, and if there is no corn near it, it doesn't get pollinated as well.

This even correlates to how corn would grow in the wild. If you put a viable husk with kernels on it out in a field, it will grow dozens of little shoots in a clump, from each of the kernels. This ensures that the plant will be near to other corn and be able to pollinate fully.

Obviously there is still pollination from the wind. but It's not the effective way to grow corn.
